discovered_by: Reverse-engineering the site's React frontend bundle (create-react-app, /championships/static/js/main.*.js) - inspecting network requests and grepping the minified source for API client methods. No official docs, no API key, no published rate limit.

endpoints.description: All available regulation sets, with the date range of tournaments known for each.
List of tournaments for one regulation set. {reg} must be URL-encoded (e.g. 'Champions Reg.M-B' -> 'Champions%20Reg.M-B').
Single tournament's basic info (superset of the /reg/{reg} list entry).
Pokemon usage stats for a tournament. Query param: placing_limit. Not used by this project - full decklists come from /standings instead.
Full standings including decklists - the main endpoint this project uses.

field_notes.player: See player_field_format below - not a clean identifier.
field_notes.record: "wins-losses-ties" as a single string, not separate fields.
field_notes.nat: ISO alpha-2, or the literal string 'Unknown'.
field_notes.tera_type: Empty string when not set/used, not null.
field_notes.drop: Not present on this endpoint at all (only per-round, via /standings/{playerID}).

endpoints.description: Per-round match data for one player: round, opponent, result, score, drop (bool, per round), and the pokemon revealed that round.

player_field_format.description: The `player` string in /standings responses is NOT a reliable structured identifier. Observed behavior, by tournament id prefix:
player_field_format.vr_prefixed_tournaments: Usually "DisplayName\nNativeID" (split on newline). BUT the ID half is not always a stable Battlefy ObjectId - it sometimes falls back to a raw display name/nickname (spaces, unicode, punctuation, emoji-like text all observed).
player_field_format.non_vr_tournaments: No separator at all - the whole field is just the display name, with no stable ID whatsoever.
player_field_format.consequence: This project always sanitizes the derived native ID to [a-zA-Z0-9_-] before using it as a DB key / filename / URL segment (see _safe_id_component in pokestats.py), and disambiguates same-tournament collisions by appending the entrant's placing.
known_quirks_observed: vr_tr_20260711 ('The Grand Champions Festival Encore', 4253 entrants): two different entrants both resolved to the literal ID 'Jack B'.
Various tournaments: native IDs seen as raw names like 'Colin/Chloe Patterson' (contains a slash), 'kaos :D' (colon + space), 'Alex S.' etc.

sprite_url_pattern.slug_rule: name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '') - lowercase, strip everything except a-z, 0-9, and hyphen. NOTE: this is a different rule from Limitless's own sprite slugs (which insert hyphens for spaces) - the two are not interchangeable.
sprite_url_pattern.why_it_matters: Limitless's own sprite CDN (r2.limitlesstcg.net) has no Mega-Evolution sprites at all, so any Pokemon sourced from pokestats.top must use pokestats' own image host instead.

reg_to_format_mapping.description: Maps pokestats' regulation-set names to this project's short format IDs (formats.py). The regulation letter alone determines the game/franchise - see formats.py FORMAT_TO_FRANCHISE for the authoritative mapping, which applies uniformly regardless of data source (Limitless also uses these same short IDs).

scale_as_of_2026_08_03.note: Small enough that this project's sync fetches every reg's full tournament list and any missing standings in one run - no pagination/backfill logic needed, unlike the Limitless pipeline.

client_behavior.rate_limiting: No documented limit; this project throttles to ~1.5s between requests as a courtesy (see PokestatsClient in pokestats.py).
client_behavior.retries: 429 -> sleep 10s and retry; 5xx -> exponential backoff, up to 4 attempts.
